$comment: VAPP-91: the host router (catalog/host.json ops): server messages in, ops out, in order. Inputs hand-written; `expected` filled by the generator from src/host/router.ts. A conformance runner creates ONE router per flow with `extensionIds`, installs `packages` (their install issues are `installIssues`), then routes every step's message and compares the ops. VAPP-122: `records` = validateRecord(packages[package].records[kind].schema, data) → issues; `acme.hours` declares two kinds, `acme.badrecords` every schema mistake. Keys of `records` and of every `properties` are written in sorted order: the Rust core iterates its maps sorted, so the issue order is the same on every platform. VAPP-161 (format version 2): `acme.v2` uses every new key validly (formatVersion, a records: binding, the records.* functions, the three tool transports, an empty extensions list); `acme.charts` declares an extension: not available under the default catalogs, installed by the VAPP-161 flow that registers it; `acme.v2broken` makes every tools / extensions / records-source mistake; `acme.future` is a newer format version; `acme.v1` is a version-1 package: refused (eApps reads only the current format; a package without formatVersion is refused too). VAPP-180: `acme.exposes` declares `upstreams` and valid `exposes` (a records read and upsert, two action bindings, an upstream); `acme.badexposes` makes every format mistake of an exposed tool, a duplicate upstream included; `acme.exposeslist` has neither list a list. VAPP-190: `acme.queries` names two JSON records queries (`queries`) and binds them with `query=<name>` (two bindings), the router expanding each bind; `acme.badqueries` makes every queries mistake (a name, an undeclared kind, a JSON-query issue, a query that is no object, a binding naming no query; `exp:issues?query=` is no records source and passes); `acme.querieslist` has queries that is no object. VAPP-203: install reduces every template as the renderer will (`acme.badcomponents`): an unknown component, a missing or mistyped prop and a slot name at the component's entry (`/templates/<id>/components/<i>`, the reducer's message), an id no component has at every place that names it (`…/children/<j>`, `…/children/componentId`, `…/slots/<name>`, message `<id>: …`), and a component whose children, slots, on or style has the wrong shape (not reduced). Template keys are in sorted order (the Rust core's maps). `acme.charts` uses its declared extension's `Gantt`: with no definition for it the host leaves its component names open. Dogfood G (2026-11-03): `acme.badqueries` also has a query reading fields its kind lacks (`fields`: a where, group, aggregate, sort and sum on unknown fields, sum/avg on a date) and an exposed tool naming no package query: issues at the query's key and at `/exposes/<i>/run/records/query`. VAPP-221 (eApps R7, files on records): `format: "attachment"` on a string field or on a list's string `items` holds the instance's attachment route `/api/attachments/<lowercase uuid>` (relative, nothing else: no origin, query or fragment; anything else = `an attachment (/api/attachments/<id>)`); `items.format` takes the same formats, on string items only. `acme.files` declares a receipt and a list of photos; `acme.badrecords` puts a format on number items. `attachments` = recordAttachmentIds(schema, data): the ids the attachment fields reference, fields sorted, each id once in the order first met, non-refs skipped (the server checks each belongs to the app and its team).
